incidents.vector: A pro-Russia hacktivist group claimed it breached Ukrposhta servers weeks earlier and launched an overnight attack on the company's IT systems.
incidents.impact: Mobile application knocked offline with temporary service disruptions; the group claims theft of a user-information database, which Ukrposhta has not confirmed.

incidents.vector: Russian authorities used Cellebrite UFED forensic extraction technology to break into a jailed dissident's seized iPhone in June 2021 — three months after Cellebrite said it had cut Russia off.
incidents.impact: Phone data was extracted and used to build a prosecution; Citizen Lab concluded Cellebrite's design made it difficult to deny abusive customers continued use of legacy hardware.

incidents.vector: The third and final defendant, 'Snoopy' (Nathan Austad), was sentenced for a 2022 credential-stuffing attack that compromised roughly 60,000 DraftKings accounts.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole about $600,000 from ~1,600 accounts and sold access to others via criminal marketplaces; Austad received 18 months and $1.3M in restitution.

incidents.vector: Attackers made rogue SD-WAN peering connections (likely via CVE-2026-20127/20182), then exploited a zero-day (CVE-2026-20245) in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager to create a rogue root account.
incidents.impact: Gained root-level control of the SD-WAN orchestrator, enabling potential undetected visibility into the provider's internal traffic; extensive anti-forensic cleanup obscured the full scope.

incidents.victim: Fortinet FortiGate firewall users (73,932 systems, 194 countries)
incidents.vector: Mass brute-forcing and exploitation of unpatched FortiGate flaws plus a custom 'FortigateSniffer' that intercepted credentials and hashes across 24 protocols; hashes were cracked on a GPU cluster and access sold.
incidents.impact: Valid admin and SSL VPN credentials for ~73,932 firewalls exposed; confirmed compromises across government, telecom, finance and healthcare, with classified documents allegedly stolen from a Turkish NATO defense contractor.

incidents.vector: Extortion group exfiltrated confidential files; Tata confirmed a breach it detected a few weeks earlier.
incidents.impact: The group claims 200,000+ stolen documents, allegedly including Apple supplier specifications and Tesla manufacturing files; Tata says operations were unaffected.

incidents.vector: Coordinated Microsoft and law-enforcement action seized servers and domains underpinning infostealer and loader 'cybercrime-as-a-service' supply chains; Microsoft used AI to link Amadey and StealC infrastructure.
incidents.impact: 326 servers and 142 domains dismantled, 27M stolen credentials reclaimed and €41M ($47M) in crypto found; 200+ StealC/Amadey C2 domains disrupted and SocGholish backdoors removed from ~15,000 sites.

incidents.victim: Multiple tech & cybersecurity firms (Huntress, LastPass, HackerOne, Recorded Future, Jamf, Snyk, others)
incidents.vector: Attackers breached market-intelligence vendor Klue and abused its Salesforce OAuth tokens to steal customers' Salesforce CRM data.
incidents.impact: Salesforce instances of numerous firms compromised; Icarus began leaking data and warned of more victims, raising the risk of follow-on social-engineering attacks.

incidents.vector: Two UK members of the Scattered Spider crew pleaded guilty to the September 2024 intrusion into Transport for London's network.
incidents.impact: The 2024 attack disrupted services for months, exposed Oyster refund customer data, forced 28,000 staff to reset passwords in person and cost ~£29M ($38M); sentencing is set for July.

incidents.vector: Attackers stole intelligence officers' mobile contact details from a company managing the agency's mobile device management platform; activity linked to 2025 Ivanti EPMM server attacks.
incidents.impact: Names, phone numbers and email addresses of Belgian State Security Service employees were exposed.

incidents.victim: Check Point Remote Access VPN customers (dozens of organizations)
incidents.vector: A ransomware affiliate exploited CVE-2026-50751, a CVSS 9.3 authentication-bypass in Check Point VPN (IKEv1), to establish fully authenticated sessions without credentials, beginning in early May — weeks before the June disclosure.
incidents.impact: A few dozen organizations were compromised; attackers used Rclone for data exfiltration and staged ransomware. CISA issued an emergency directive on June 21.

incidents.victim: Universities and Oracle PeopleSoft users (incl. University of Nottingham)
incidents.vector: Extortion group exploited an unpatched Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day (CVE-2026-35273, added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog) to steal data since late May.
incidents.impact: Multiple universities are being extorted; data theft confirmed at the University of Nottingham, with the Oracle flaw under active exploitation.

incidents.vector: The university is rebuilding its entire IT infrastructure following a hack the prior week; details have not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: Significant IT disruption requiring a full infrastructure rebuild.

incidents.vector: Intelligence sources believe Israeli hackers were likely behind a cyberattack that crippled Iranian banks earlier in June.
Ukrainian national Oleksii Lytvynenko pleaded guilty, after extradition from Ireland, to coding a Conti malware 'loader' and handling stolen victim data (2020-2022).
incidents.impact: Conti infected 1,000+ networks across 47 US states and 31 countries, causing at least $150M in ransom payments; Lytvynenko faces up to 20 years in prison.
